claims.text: Accelerated free-energy methods such as umbrella sampling can generate mappings suitable for tailoring thermal treatments in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Free-energy-informed thermal schedules will control phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Such schedules selectively lower kinetic barriers for desired phase transformations.
Lowering the kinetic barriers will promote a more uniform and stable phase composition.
The initial Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy has a multiphase microstructure containing both equilibrium and metastable phases.
Free-energy landscape mappings permit precise selection of temperature ramps and annealing schedules.
Computed free-energy barriers can be used to select annealing temperature, dwell time, and cooling rate.
Accelerated sampling elucidates kinetic barriers associated with phase transformations in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Accelerated sampling identifies thermodynamic basins associated with different phase transformations.
Umbrella-sampling maps can be used to optimize thermal treatment to reduce unwanted metastable-phase formation.
Adjusted heating and cooling protocols lower kinetic constraints that lead to phase heterogeneity.
Reducing those kinetic constraints stabilizes the desired equilibrium phases.
The intervention will produce a more uniform phase distribution favoring targeted equilibrium phases.
The resulting microstructure may improve mechanical and thermal performance relative to conventional processing.
Standard thermal treatments that do not use detailed free-energy landscapes often produce broader phase distributions and more metastable phases.
The intervention is most effective when thermal treatment dominates phase evolution.
Severe processing such as extensive mechanical alloying may override thermally driven phase-control mechanisms.
